name: The penitent thief
summary: Two malefactors were crucified with Christ, one on either side, and one of them railed on him while the other rebuked his fellow, owned that they received the due reward of their deeds, and said that this man had done nothing amiss (Luke 23:32-33; Luke 23:39-41). He then asked to be remembered when Christ came into his kingdom, which is not the speech of a man who thought him a common prisoner (Luke 23:42). He was answered with the promise of paradise that same day (Luke 23:43).
offenseFull: Two other malefactors were led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary, one criminal on the right hand and one on the left (Luke 23:32-33). The soldiers mocked him and offered him vinegar, the superscription over him was written in letters of Greek and Latin and Hebrew, and one of the two railed on him, telling him to save himself and them if he was the Christ (Luke 23:36-39). The other rebuked his companion, asked whether he did not fear God seeing he was under the same condemnation, said that they were there justly and received the due reward of their deeds, and that this man had done nothing amiss (Luke 23:40-41). He did not use his own suffering as an argument for his innocence. He judged himself first, and he judged his fellow for railing.

Then he asked to be remembered when Christ came into his kingdom (Luke 23:42). That petition tells what the man already knew. A prisoner who thought this was just another condemned man would not have spoken of a kingdom that was coming. The rulers of his nation had said they had no king but Caesar (John 19:15), having settled into their place under Rome and their share of its comfort; this man, with nothing left and hours to live, was still looking for the kingdom the scriptures promised. He had broken Rome’s law and Rome was killing him for it. His repentance showed itself in the rebuke he gave, the guilt he owned and the mercy he asked for.
judgmentFull: The answer was that he would be with him that day in paradise (Luke 23:43). The promise did not take him off the cross and did not declare his former deeds harmless. Nor is it a general rule that every man goes somewhere at death. Esdras was told he would be taken away from all and would remain with the Son and with such as were like him until the times were ended (2 Esdras 14:9), and Christ said that where he is, there also shall his servant be (John 12:26). John saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, speaking, asking how long until their blood was avenged, receiving white robes and told to rest yet for a little season (Revelation 6:9-11), while the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished (Revelation 20:5). The righteous is taken away from the evil to come, and enters into peace (Isaiah 57:1-2). The promise is particular, and it was spoken over a man who had just acknowledged that his punishment was just.

Isaiah had written that the servant would be numbered with the transgressors and make intercession for the transgressors (Isaiah 53:12), and here is the scene in the flesh: the innocent man between two guilty ones, the one railing and the other receiving mercy. There was darkness over all the earth from the sixth hour to the ninth, the sun was darkened and the veil of the temple was rent, and when it was over the centurion glorified God and said that certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that had come to the sight beat their breasts and went home (Luke 23:44-48). The last hour was not out of reach of repentance. It is no warrant for counting on a last hour that has not been promised to anybody.

lawsResolved.text: A thief is cursed by God and to be cut off from the people.
Confession and repentance necessary to pardon sin and for God to release us from His chastisements and punishments.
Unless you repent you will perish.

text.text: And there were also two other, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.
And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,
And saying, If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.
And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.
But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?
And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.
And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.
And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
For thou shalt be taken away from all, and from henceforth thou shalt remain with my Son, and with such as be like thee, until the times be ended.
If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will my Father honour.
And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held:
And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?

And white robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled.
But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.
The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.
He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.

Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.
And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.
And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.
Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.
And all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts, and returned.
Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.
The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.
And with him they crucify two thieves; the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.
